:::{#exm-equivalent-cycle}
#### Three equivalent statements
<!-- no-figure: a short chain of implications; nothing to plot -->

Let $n$ be an [integer](number-systems.qmd#def-integers),
and let:

- $P_1$ be "$n$ is [even](number-systems.qmd#def-even-odd)";
- $P_2$ be "$n + 1$ is [odd](number-systems.qmd#def-odd)";
- $P_3$ be "$n + 2$ is even".

If $n = 2m$,
then $n + 1 = 2m + 1$,
so $P_1 \Rightarrow P_2$.
If $n + 1 = 2m + 1$,
then $n + 2 = 2(m + 1)$,
so $P_2 \Rightarrow P_3$.
If $n + 2 = 2m$,
then $n = 2(m - 1)$,
so $P_3 \Rightarrow P_1$.
By [a cycle of conditionals](#thm-equivalent-cycle),
the three [propositions](#def-proposition) are all true or all false.
Three conditionals were enough,
where checking each pair both ways would take six.

:::
